prompt:
You are formalizing a provision of US tax law (26 USC § 7701) into OCaml.

## Input format

You receive a provision of US tax law as text. Some sub-provisions are already formalized as
OCaml code and appear in ```<sub-provision-code> ... ```</sub-provision-code> fences — these are
your helper functions. Call them by name in your function body. Do NOT rewrite or rename them.
Sub-provisions shown as plain text have not been formalized; incorporate their meaning directly
into your function body as conditions, branches, or values.

## Patterns

Pattern 1 — disjunction: any child being true qualifies the entity. Use ||.
  let is_regulated_public_utility (entity : entity) : bool =
    furnishes_electricity entity ||
    transports_gas_pipeline entity ||
    transports_gas_rail entity

Pattern 2 — conjunction: all children must hold simultaneously. Use &&.
  let is_cooperative_bank (institution : institution) : bool =
    no_capital_stock institution &&
    organized_cooperatively institution

Pattern 3 — conditional: same term defined differently based on a condition.
  let meaning_of_delegate (ref_official : official) : delegate =
    if refers_to_secretary ref_official then meaning_of_delegate_secretary ref_official
    else meaning_of_delegate_other ref_official

Pattern 4 — arithmetic: formula producing a numeric value.
  let cost_ratio (foreign_cost : money) (total_cost : money) : decimal =
    foreign_cost /. total_cost

Pattern 5 — mixed: condition selects which computation applies.
  let material_assistance_ratio (facility : facility) : decimal =
    if is_qualified_facility facility then cost_ratio_b facility
    else cost_ratio_c facility

Pattern 6 — wrapper: no computation; provision groups independent sub-provisions.
Write a module grouping the child functions. Do not add any computation.
  module Delegate = struct
    let meaning_of_delegate_secretary (ref_official : official) : delegate = ...
    let meaning_of_delegate_other (ref_official : official) : delegate = ...
  end

Pattern 7 — partial: sub-expression that only completes at parent level.
  (* total_direct_costs_of_prohibited_products : money
     — partial expression, computation completes at parent level *)

## Rules

- snake_case function names derived from the term or header
- Inputs named from provision text (entity, institution, person, facility, etc.)
- Do not invent conditions, types, or formulas absent from the provision text
- Write only the OCaml skeleton — use descriptive placeholder names for sub-conditions
- Declare all types (type, variant, record) before any function that uses them
- Declare all helper functions before the function that calls them
- Use `let ... in` for helpers needed only inside one function — do not promote them to top level
- Prefer `match` over `if/else` when dispatching on variant types
- Boolean predicates: prefix with `is_` or `has_`. Value-returning functions: noun prefix (e.g. `delegate_of`, `cost_of`)
- Keep function names short and idiomatic — avoid restating the full statutory phrase
- Inline trivial one-line logic; only extract a helper when it is reused or meaningfully named
- Add brief OCaml comments (`(* ... *)`) on types and functions explaining what statutory concept they capture
- Use `option` for values that may be absent
- Do not use training knowledge to resolve cross-referenced sections
- Float operators for ratios/amounts: <. >. <=. >=. +. -. *. /. (not integer operators)
- If a sub-provision references an external section of law that cannot be resolved, write a
  stub function with the correct input/output signature and a comment body marking it unresolved:
    let is_qualified_facility (facility : facility) : bool =
      (* unresolved — needs §45Y(b)(1), §48E(b)(3) *)
      failwith "unresolved cross-reference"
  Set pattern "ambiguous" and name the needed sections in reason. Continue formalizing the
  parent — use the stub function in your composition as if it were resolved.
- If a sibling sub-provision (already formalized as OCaml in the input) provides the missing
  section that a stub depends on, replace the stub with a direct call to that sibling's function.
- If the overall computation is unspecified or fully delegated, set pattern "ambiguous",
  ocaml "", explain in reason.

## Output

Return JSON only, no prose, no markdown fences:
{"ocaml": "the ocaml code", "pattern": "disjunction|conjunction|conditional|arithmetic|mixed|wrapper|partial|ambiguous", "reason": "one sentence"}

7701(b)(6) — Lawful permanent resident
For purposes of this subsection, an individual is a lawful permanent resident of the United States at any time if—

7701(b)(6)(A)
such individual has the status of having been lawfully accorded the privilege of residing permanently in the United States as an immigrant in accordance with the immigration laws, and

7701(b)(6)(B)
such status has not been revoked (and has not been administratively or judicially determined to have been abandoned).
An individual shall cease to be treated as a lawful permanent resident of the United States if such individual commences to be treated as a resident of a foreign country under the provisions of a tax treaty between the United States and the foreign country, does not waive the benefits of such treaty applicable to residents of the foreign country, and notifies the Secretary of the commencement of such treatment.

Write an OCaml function for provision 7701(b)(6).

  waived_treaty_benefits : bool; (* flush: waived treaty benefits applicable to residents of foreign country *)
  notified_secretary_of_treaty_treatment : bool; (* flush: notified Secretary of commencement of such treatment *)

(* (A) and (B): individual currently holds unrevoked, non-abandoned immigrant status *)
let has_current_lawful_permanent_status (individual : individual) : bool =
  individual.has_immigrant_status &&
  not individual.status_revoked &&
  not individual.status_abandoned

(* flush language: treaty-based cessation of lawful permanent resident treatment *)
let has_ceased_via_treaty (individual : individual) : bool =
